title: A Moray Eel Has a Second Set of Jaws Inside Its Throat

scenes.text: A moray eel has a second set of jaws inside its throat.
First, its normal jaws bite the prey.
Then another jaw, lined with teeth, shoots forward out of the throat.
It grabs the prey and drags it down toward the stomach.
Morays live in tight rock cracks, so they can't suck food in like other fish.
So they evolved a second mouth. Yes, really.

description:
A moray eel has a second set of toothed jaws in its throat that launch into its mouth to pull prey down.
Researchers filmed it in slow motion at UC Davis.
Which animal feature scares you most?
